## Description

Generates profile likelihood confidence intervals
for standardized regression coefficients (beta) and other effect sizes,
including multiple correlation, semipartial correlations,
improvement in R-squared, squared partial correlations,
differences in standardized regression coefficients,
and Cohen's f-squared, for models fitted by `lm()`.
The intervals invert the Gaussian likelihood-ratio test
of the covariance matrix of the outcome and the regressors,
with a normal-theory or a robust (fourth-moment) cutoff.

## Installation

You can install the development version of `betaLB` from
[GitHub](https://github.com/jeksterslab/betaLB) with:

```r
if (!require("pak")) install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("jeksterslab/betaLB")
```

## Example

In this example, a multiple regression model is fitted
using program quality ratings (`QUALITY`) as the regressand/outcome variable
and number of published articles attributed to the program faculty members (`NARTIC`),
percent of faculty members holding research grants (`PCTGRT`), and
percentage of program graduates who received support (`PCTSUPP`) as regressor/predictor variables
using a data set from 1982 ratings of 46 doctoral programs in psychology in the USA [@NationalResearchCouncil-1982].
Likelihood-based confidence intervals for the standardized regression coefficients are generated
using the `BetaLB()` function from the `betaLB` package.

```{r}
#| message = FALSE
library(package = betaLB)
```

```{r}
#| echo = FALSE
if (!exists(x = "nas1982")) {
  try(
    expr = utils::data(
      "nas1982",
      package = "betaLB"
    ),
    silent = TRUE
  )
}
df <- nas1982
```

```{r}
df <- betaLB::nas1982
```

### Fit the regression model using the `lm()` function.

```{r}
object <- stats::lm(formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP, data = df)
```

### Estimate the standardized regression slopes and the corresponding likelihood-based confidence intervals.

```{r}
BetaLB(object = object, type = "mvn", alpha = 0.05)
```

## Other Features

The package provides the following functions.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `BetaLB()` | Standardized regression coefficients with normal-theory (`type = "mvn"`) or robust (`type = "robust"`) likelihood intervals |
| `RSqLB()` | R-squared and adjusted R-squared |
| `DiffBetaLB()` | Differences of standardized regression coefficients |
| `SCorLB()` | Semipartial correlations |
| `SCorSqLB()` | Squared semipartial correlations (squared signed interval) |
| `PCorLB()` | Squared partial correlations |
| `DeltaRSqLB()` | Improvement in R-squared |
| `FSqLB()` | Cohen's f-squared and local f-squared |

The `coef()`, `confint()`, `summary()`, and `print()` methods
are available for the returned objects.
The effect-size functions take the output of `BetaLB()`
and use its `type` and `control`.
Scalar targets use profile-likelihood regions;
multi-coefficient targets use a conservative vector projection,
and the output names the calibration and its dimension.
An unverified endpoint is `NA`; no Wald endpoint is substituted.
Robust calibration assumes independently sampled random regressors
and finite fourth moments.
Examples for each function are in the package vignettes.

## Effect Sizes

The definitions, formulas, and notes on the intervals
are in the help pages of the functions
and in the vignette
[betaLB: Example Using the Effect Size Functions](https://jeksterslab.github.io/betaLB/articles/example-es-lb.html).
